market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner-operator or farm manager of an oyster / abalone / mussel / seaweed farm. Typically the family-owner principal with a deckhand or two; for larger players (Yumbah, Australia's Oyster Coast, Tasmanian Oyster Co), the operations/production manager.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Approximately 400-550 shellfish/aquaculture farm businesses in Australia. NSW: ~270 Class-A aquaculture permits across 31 estuaries (~3,000 ha). Tasmania: 43 oyster growers (Oysters Tasmania). South Australia: ~100-130 oyster growers across Coffin Bay, Smoky Bay, Streaky Bay, Cowell. Plus ~10-15 commercial abalone farms (Yumbah, Jade Tiger, Great Southern Waters, etc.), small mussel and seaweed segments. National GVP for oyster industry ~AUD $106M (2018-19, growing); aquaculture industry revenue AUD $2.8B (2024-25, IBISWorld).
market_sizing.business_count_global: Globally tens of thousands of shellfish farms. US ~1,700-2,000 shellfish farms (NOAA); France ~3,000 oyster producers; UK ~400; Canada ~600; New Zealand ~120 oyster + ~250 mussel/salmon. Asia dominates volume (China, Korea) but is largely informal/co-op organised. Reachable English-speaking SMB TAM ~6,000-8,000 farms.
market_sizing.typical_size: 1-15 employees; AUD $200k-$5M annual revenue. Family-run farms dominate; consolidators like Yumbah and Australia's Oyster Coast aggregate dozens of leases under one corporate parent.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: Oceanfarmr (AU-NZ founded, global): tiered by farm size, not publicly listed at named tiers but third-party indications place small-farm plans around AUD $50-150/mo and larger multi-site at AUD $300-800/mo. miShell (AU, SA): annual subscription priced by peak stock holdings — small farms ~AUD $1,000-2,500/yr (~AUD $85-200/mo); larger multi-farm tiers higher with multi-farm discount. OysterTracker (US, ~15 clients at launch): undisclosed; FindMyOyster, Ozrit, KAMAHU all custom-quoted. No incumbent has publicly listed enterprise pricing.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AUD $80-$250/mo for SMB single-farm; AUD $300-$700/mo for multi-lease/corporate. AU willingness is constrained — many farms still use spreadsheets and paper. Apply ~70% of US benchmarks; commodity-margin business compresses WTP further than land-based ag.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Founder-led + community sales. Reference selling through growers' associations. Cannot be self-serve only — onboarding (mapping leases, baskets, baskets-per-line) requires hand-holding.
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Modest-to-moderate. Embedded payments on wholesale invoicing to merchants/restaurants; traceability QR/consumer-story add-on (premium); environmental monitoring hardware bundling (margin on probes); export-certificate automation (per-shipment fee); insurance partner referrals on POMS/storm loss. 1.5-2x ARPU expansion realistic, capped by farm-revenue ceiling.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Oceanfarmr (AU/NZ origin, broad species coverage — oyster, mussel, seaweed, salmon; raised seed funding; iOS/Android + web dashboard; most polished UX in the segment); miShell (AU, SA-built by oyster farmers, stock-tier pricing, very farmer-friendly, narrower feature set); OysterTracker (US-based, launched 2023-2024, ~15 clients AU+US at launch); FindMyOyster (US, integrates with FDA/state DOH for HACCP/shellstock tags, mostly US-centric); Ozrit (positioning as enterprise, multi-site, hatchery + grow-out); KAMAHU (fish-focused, less oyster); Excel/Google Sheets remains the de facto incumbent — Oceanfarmr explicitly offers a free farm-management spreadsheet as a lead magnet, acknowledging the spreadsheet baseline.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: Oceanfarmr founded ~2016-2017 (~9 years); miShell ~2017-2018; OysterTracker ~2023-2024 (very new); FindMyOyster ~2019. Segment is YOUNG — no 20-year incumbent to dethrone, but also low product maturity to leapfrog.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Public review surface is THIN (no Capterra or G2 review density for Oceanfarmr/miShell/OysterTracker — telling on its own). Industry articles (Oceanfarmr's own blog, Ozrit) flag the pain: 'Many established oyster farming enterprises continue to operate on fragmented spreadsheet systems, outdated desktop software, or generic agricultural platforms that were never designed for shellfish aquaculture, creating compounding risks including regulatory exposure, production losses from poor data visibility, and inability to scale.' FRDC reports note traceability and labour-tracking pain. Reddit/forum complaints sparse — farmers are not heavy online community users compared with, say, software developers or wineries.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Premium Shellfish (US, automated oyster operations) raised USD $18M Series A led by Cavallo Ventures early 2026 — strongest oyster-specific signal. Aquabyte raised USD $22M growth round 2025 (fish health, computer vision). Australian Government pledged AUD $15M to Queensland aquaculture sector in 2024-2025. Overall aquaculture VC was USD $619M in 2024 (down 28% YoY); software took 27% of VC in 2023. No major M&A among the dedicated oyster-SaaS incumbents; segment is too small to attract roll-ups yet.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Low-to-moderate. Computer-vision sizing/grading, AI water-quality alerting, and AI demand forecasting are being piloted (Aquabyte fish, Premium Shellfish automation), but no AI-native oyster-ops SaaS dominant yet. Window is wider here than dental/wine (24-36 months) because the buyer is harder to reach and slower to adopt.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Stock tracking by basket / line / bag through grow-out stages (spat → juvenile → market), grading and movement events on the water, harvest and shellstock-tag traceability, environmental closures (heavy-rain, biotoxin, fecal coliform) interrupting harvest, labour timesheets on boats, and wholesale invoicing to restaurants/merchants. Today this lives in waterproof notebooks, whiteboards, Excel and SMS. Critical workflow on a Tasmanian or NSW oyster farm during a POMS scare or rain closure is paper-based, with no real-time stock view across leases.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Shellstock-tag traceability (FDA/NSW Food Authority compliance) + integration with state health portals; environmental data integration (BoM, state DPI rain gauges, biotoxin testing labs); data network effects from grower co-operatives; switching cost via multi-year stock-lineage history; lease-mapping IP.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Xero/MYOB (AU accounting); Stripe/Square for wholesale invoicing; state shellfish quality assurance portals (NSW Food Authority Shellfish Program, SASQAP for SA, TSQAP for Tasmania); Bureau of Meteorology rainfall API; biotoxin testing lab feeds; Australia Post/StarTrack/cold-chain freight; export documentation portals; basic IoT (water-temperature, salinity probes).
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: None. No incumbent ERP owns this data. Greenfield rip-and-replace possible because most farms have no software at all.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: High and idiosyncratic. Each state runs its own shellfish quality assurance program (NSW Shellfish Program, TSQAP, SASQAP, WA, VIC). Harvest area classifications, recall procedures, shellstock tagging, biotoxin closures, faecal coliform thresholds, POMS movement permits (TAS Biosecurity Act 2019) all differ. SafeFish 2025-2030 program coordinates technical responses but each jurisdiction enforces independently.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: EU Fisheries Control Regulation: from Jan 2026, EU-bound seafood requires digital catch & lot data — direct tailwind for any AU exporter selling to EU. SafeFish 2025-2030 program launched (UTAS + SARDI partnership), driving traceability uplift. Nov 2025 Aus Government announcement to 'dig deeper into data on imported seafood' signals broader traceability scrutiny. TSQAP and NSW Shellfish Program continue periodic updates. Yumbah's BAP certification (first AU oyster producer) creates an emerging premium-market expectation for software-supported traceability. No single hard cliff date in AU but EU Jan 2026 + BAP/MSC trend = real forcing function for exporters.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: Very high. Oyster vs abalone vs mussel workflows differ materially; tidal/lease/longline mechanics, POMS biosecurity, faecal coliform/QA closures, shellstock tag chain-of-custody, harvest area classification (Approved/Restricted/Prohibited) all require either embedded co-founder or close 6-12 month immersion. Hardest of the three options for an outsider.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 6-9 months for a credible MVP (stock by lease/line/basket, grading events, harvest with shellstock tags, environmental closure alerts, Xero export). Multi-state QA portal integration extends to 12+ months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Offline-first mobile UX (poor reception on the water); GPS/mapping of leases and lines; integrating with state QA portals that have no public API; environmental data ingestion reliability; tag printing on ruggedised hardware; QR-code traceability that survives cold/wet handling.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Yes — high. NSW, TAS, SA, VIC, WA each run separate Shellfish QA programs with different classifications, sampling regimes, and reporting requirements. Multiple rule engines needed. Critical to launch in 1-2 states first (likely SA + TAS where miShell + Oceanfarmr have proven a market).
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Soft. No strict AU-only mandate but state government portals favour AU-hosted partners. Easy to satisfy.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: Growers' associations (NSW Farmers Oyster Section, Oysters Tasmania, SA Oyster Growers Association, OISAS, Oysters Australia peak body), FRDC funded events, Australian Aquaculture Conference, Seafood Directions, regional grower meetings, SafeFish newsletter, partnerships with hatcheries (Shellfish Culture, Cameron of Tasmania, Eyre Peninsula) for referrals, paid Facebook (high penetration among rural SMBs), cold outbound (lease licences are public registers).
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 6-8 active: Oysters Australia (peak), Oysters Tasmania, NSW Farmers Oyster Section / NSW Oysters, SA Oyster Growers Association, Australian Abalone Growers Association, Australian Mussel Industry Association, plus state-level seafood industry bodies.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: 3-4: Australasian Aquaculture magazine, National Aquaculture Council newsletters, FRDC Fish magazine, SeafoodSource (international). Modest paid-sponsorship surface.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 3-5 viable annual events: Australasian Aquaculture (biennial, ~$10k for booth), Seafood Directions (biennial), state grower AGMs, FRDC events. Tight but workable budget.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: Moderate-to-high. NSW, TAS, SA aquaculture lease registers are public; ASIC business search; growers' association directories; phone numbers and farm-gate addresses generally listed. Less email-discoverable than dental — many farms use generic Gmail or just phone.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Low-to-moderate. Oyster farmers are tight-knit communities skeptical of city outsiders — miShell explicitly markets 'built by South Australian oyster farmers for farmers' which is the playbook here. Hardest founder-market fit of the three; almost certainly needs a domain co-founder or paid grower advisory board.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Higher than dental/wine. Realistic 5 reference customers in 6-9 months if anchored to one estuary/region; faster with a grower co-founder or association partnership.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Very low. 'Oyster farm software Australia' is barely a search market. SEO will be slow because intent volume is low; trade-press features and word-of-mouth dominate. Achievable to rank but limited inbound demand.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Moderate. State shellfish QA programs effectively gatekeep operating data but participate via reporting templates rather than locked APIs. Hatcheries are upstream gatekeepers for spat supply — partnering with them is high-leverage.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~40-50%. Reuse: inventory (stock by location), bin/locations (lease → line → basket maps cleanly to nested locations), suppliers (hatcheries, equipment), activity log, BOM (less applicable but usable for input-cost tracking), production orders (loosely as 'harvest events'). New: lease GPS mapping, basket/line stock lineage with mortality, grading events, shellstock-tag generation, environmental/closure events, offline-first mobile.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Tenant, RLS, auth, server actions, design system, activity log, bin-aisle uniqueness pattern (directly relevant for lease/line/basket hierarchy). Offline-first PWA / native mobile required new.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Low. Aquaculture buyers do not overlap Manuva manufacturing customers. Fresh GTM required.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Medium-low. Stock-tracking and traceability concepts transfer but the field operations (boats, leases, tides) and biology (mortality, growth curves) are foreign to manufacturing.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 18-24 months. Workflow alone is replicable; durable moat comes from state QA portal integrations, grower-association relationships, and accumulated lease/line lineage data — these take years.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Moderate concern. Heavy support load (rural customers, low computer literacy in some segments) erodes margin; offline-mobile QA/edge cases add engineering cost; SMS for closure alerts is pass-through but adds friction. Expect 70-78% gross margin (below SaaS 85% benchmark) without disciplined self-serve onboarding.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Yes — many growers run multiple leases across estuaries; consolidators (Australia's Oyster Coast, Yumbah) run 10+ sites. Multi-lease pricing is a natural expansion lever.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Moderate. POMS / storm / heat events can wipe out a farm; small operators occasionally exit. High switching cost once lineage history accumulates but the buyer pool naturally shrinks during disease events. Counterbalanced by the consolidator trend lifting per-customer ARPU.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: ~400-500 customers at AUD $2-2.5k ARR to hit AUD $1M ARR — which would be ~80-100% of the addressable AU farm count. Implies global expansion (US, NZ, UK, France) is mandatory to reach $1M ARR. Realistic for a niche but constrains the venture-scale upside.
